newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Scientists to discuss easing British beef ban.
newsitem.headline: Scientists to discuss easing British beef ban.

text.p: Independent scientific veterinary experts are expected to give an opinion on Wednesday on a Britain's bid to ease a worldwide ban on its beef exports by exempting herds certified to be free of mad cow disease.

Britain proposed in February that the ban, which was imposed in March 1996, should be be partially lifted to allow exports of beef from Northern Irish and other herds guaranteed to be free of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).
The ban was imposed after Britain said that BSE could be transmitted to humans who ate infected beef.
Northern Irish herds would be the first to benefit because their movements have been tracked by computer records for the past eight years unlike those in Scotland and England.

If the scientists' opinion is positive, Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler could draw up a proposal on the certified herds scheme which would be sent to the EU Standing Veterinary Committee of senior member state officials.
If there was a qualified majority in favour of easing the ban, the Commission could then act on it.
Commission officials said it was difficult to predict how long the process would take.
